Thanks — draft below (lean, math + choices). My assumptions: tokenization using our standard UTF-8 tokenizer, invoice-level aggregation daily, and minimums applied monthly.

Proposal (send to customer):

1) Rounding / Metering
- We meter at the request level but aggregate per-customer per-day for billing accuracy. Invoices are generated monthly.
- Rounding rule: we apply tokenization then round usage to the nearest whole billing unit (our billing quantum = 1 token). We do NOT round up to a larger slab per-request — instead we total all tokens across the month and bill on the aggregated total. Example (from your sample):
  - If day 1 total tokens = 1,234.3 and day 2 = 2,876.7, monthly total = 4,111.0 => billed tokens = 4,111.

2) Minimums & Commit Ladder (how credits work)
- Commit bands: small (0–100k/mo), mid (100–500k/mo), large (>500k/mo). Each band has an effective floor equal to 50% of committed tokens in month 1, ramping to 100% after month 3 (standard onboarding ramp).
- If actual billed tokens < monthly floor, we issue credit equal to (floor - billed) * unit_price. Credits applied to future invoices for up to 6 months.

3) Grace/washout options (choose one)
A. 30-day pilot grace (default): no true-up for months 1–2; credits accrue but won’t be invoiced for 30 days after contract start. Good for tight pilots.
B. 90-day extended grace + one-time onboarding credit: treat months 1–3 as ramp window; any shortfall converted to a one-time credit (applied to next invoice) and no enforcement until month 4. We can offer a 10% onboarding credit if they commit to a 6-month paid pilot.

4) SOW language snippet to include in NOVA_SOW_v2.pdf (we should attach small excerpt):
- "Billing: charges computed on monthly aggregated token usage. Minimums apply per commit band. Shortfalls during the onboarding window will be credited as described in the Contract Schedule. Credits may be applied to subsequent invoices for up to 6 months."

Flags for Legal/Finance:
- Need to confirm: do we allow credits to exceed 100% of first invoice? (I recommend no.)
- Confirm SLA credits interplay with billing credits (separate).

If that looks good I’ll convert to plain language and include a small sample invoice using their CSV.

—Ben
Ben Carter

Subject: RE: Clarify commit/grace-period and rounding ladder for NOVACorp pilot

Hi Claire —

Thanks for the sample file. Quick summary of how the POC billing would work (short version you can share with internal stakeholders):

- Metering: we tokenize each request and aggregate per-customer monthly. Billing quantum = 1 token; we round after monthly aggregation (we do NOT round at the per-request level).

- Commit ladder & minimums: commits map into bands (small, mid, large). For pilots we default to a 50% floor in month 1 that ramps to 100% by month 3. If actual usage falls below the monthly floor we issue a credit = (floor - billed_tokens) * unit_price; credits apply to subsequent invoices (valid up to 6 months).

- Grace options: two options we can include in the SOW —
  1) 30-day pilot grace: minimal administrative overhead; shortfalls credited and can be applied as described.
  2) 90-day ramp + onboarding credit: treats months 1–3 as onboarding; any shortfall is a one-time credit and we offer a 10% onboarding credit if you commit to 6 months.

I’ve attached an updated SOW excerpt (NOVA_SOW_v2.pdf) and a sample invoice showing how the numbers in your CSV would map to billed tokens and credits.

Next step: if you prefer option 2 (90-day), let me know and we’ll mark that in the SOW and route to Legal for the onboarding credit. If you want the sample invoice broken down by day/model, I can ask Ben to produce that.

Best —
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
Attachment: NOVA_SOW_v2.pdf (application/pdf), sample_invoice_preview.pdf (application/pdf)
